step-1.text: Lay one side panel flat on the floor, holes up. Screw in four cam pins at the top and middle, and press six dowels into the rest of the holes.

count-1.text: This step uses 1 side panel, 4 cam pins and 6 wood dowels.

step-2.text: Push the bottom panel onto the low dowels. Then drive two screws through the outside of the side panel into it.

count-2.text: This step uses 1 fixed panel and 2 screws.

step-3.text: Slide the fixed middle panel onto its pins. Drop in two cam locks, arrows toward the pins, and turn them clockwise.

count-3.text: This step uses 1 fixed panel and 2 cam locks.

step-4.text: Same move for the top panel. Push it onto the pins, two cam locks, clockwise.

count-4.text: This step uses 1 fixed panel and 2 cam locks.

step-5.text: Now the other ends. Pins and dowels go in the same pattern, so the second side can drop straight on.

count-5.text: This step uses 4 cam pins and 6 wood dowels.

step-6.text: With a helper, lower the second side onto all the pins at once. Two screws at the bottom, then lock the last four cam locks.

count-6.text: This step uses 1 side panel, 2 screws and 4 cam locks.

step-7.text: Tap four dowels into the ends of the plinth board, and press it in under the bottom panel at the front.

count-7.text: This step uses 1 plinth and 4 wood dowels.

step-8.text: Roll the frame over so it lies face down. Ask your helper. It's long.

count-8.text: Nothing new this step. Just you and the frame.

step-9.text: Lay the first back half on, shiny side in. Line it up with the bottom corners, then nail it along the edges every fifteen centimeters or so.

count-9.text: This step uses 1 back panel and 16 nails.

step-10.text: Second back half, butted tight to the first. Same nailing pattern. Keep the frame square while you go.

count-10.text: This step uses 1 back panel and 16 nails.

step-11.text: Stand the bookcase up together. Lift with your legs, not your back.

count-11.text: Nothing new this step. Just you and the frame.

step-12.text: Pick your shelf heights. Push four shelf pins in at each height, two on each side, all at the same level.

step-13.text: Tilt each shelf in and lay it flat on its pins. Four shelves, no tools.

step-14.text: Last one, and the most important. Screw the two wall brackets to the top, and fix them to the wall with screws that suit your wall.

done.text: Bookcase built. Fourteen steps, all yours. Now the hard part: picking which books go up top.
